subject: Data entry / keying / data capture services
reason: Precision v2 retains 57 historical notices across 35 buyers. QA includes explicit open-bid Data Capture Services requiring data entry on an as-requested basis with error-rate, security and turnaround requirements, plus explicit 'Saisie de données'. Seven records are title-led digital-first; the broader family includes scope-only noise and remains visible separately.
model_implication: Extremely automatable information-in→structured-output work. Main risks are data security/residency, accuracy guarantees and buyer-specific tooling rather than production labor.

subject: Evidence / literature synthesis and rapid evidence review
reason: 37 precision notices across 28 buyers; 13 title-led digital-first. QA includes an open competitive PHAC requirement for rapid, high-quality, fit-for-purpose evidence synthesis products. Other records can require PhD/domain expertise or qualified engineers, so expert-credential burden must be assessed at opportunity level.
model_implication: AI can compress search, screening, extraction, synthesis and formatting dramatically; human domain review may be the scarce credential layer rather than the bulk labor.

subject: Desk research / benchmarking
reason: 17 precision notices across 15 buyers; 3 title-led digital-first and 14 scope-led digital-first. QA includes an explicit Belgian desk-research study on global credit-insurance/surety markets and market-research frameworks where desk research is a defined delivery phase.
model_implication: Strong agentic-research + analyst-QA fit; likely more defensible where deliverable is structured market intelligence rather than primary field research.

subject: Data collection / research services
reason: 48 precision notices across 42 buyers; 36 title-led digital-first. QA includes FRANET data-collection and research services plus reading-program pilot research. The family is real but can mix remote desk/data collection with interviews/fieldwork.
model_implication: Potentially strong if data collection is web/document/remote; fieldwork-heavy subsets should be demoted or subcontracted.

subject: Data cleaning / enrichment / Master Data Management
reason: 50 precision notices across 34 buyers; 27 title-led digital-first. QA shows genuine MDM/data-quality procurements from the National Bank of Belgium, Infrabel and Czech Post. Some scope-only matches are broad research/advisory or enterprise-platform programs, so the lean opportunity is the data-operation subset, not automatically all MDM implementations.
model_implication: Very strong AI/data-pipeline edge when the output is cleaning, normalization, dedupe, enrichment or QA; much weaker when the contract is enterprise MDM platform implementation.

subject: Content / data migration as a single lean business lane
reason: 165 precision notices and 44 title-led digital-first prove a real migration market. QA also shows many large SAP/KIS/platform implementations where migration is only one component. Pure migration examples exist (e.g. specialized conversion/migration advice; migration to Microsoft Fabric), but the 165-record family is not uniformly lean.
next_test: Split PURE_DATA_MIGRATION from PLATFORM_IMPLEMENTATION_WITH_MIGRATION and compare bidders/winners/tickets.

subject: Metadata / cataloguing / indexing — precision subset
reason: The 904-record v1 broad family was rejected because generic procurement 'catalogue' wording dominated. v2 strict phrases leave only 24 notices across 17 buyers, including 7 title-led digital-first. This precision subset is the only metadata/cataloguing family eligible for promotion; v1 remains recall-only.
model_implication: Small but naturally automatable; deeper QA should distinguish bibliographic/library specialization from generic metadata tagging.

subject: Document digitization services — physical-input lane
reason: 82 precision notices across 72 buyers remain after removing medical/equipment collisions. All 82 are intentionally flagged physical-input-likely. The market is real but not natively remote because paper/archive handling and custody can dominate.
model_implication: Potential broker/partner lane where SPM supplies OCR/workflow/QA while a local scanning partner handles custody and physical intake.

subject: OCR / text extraction
reason: Only 9 precision notices, with 4 title-led digital-first, survive strict v2. Mechanically this is one of SPM's strongest AI advantages, but sample size is too small for a strong historical market-size claim from this classifier alone.
next_test: Expand multilingual OCR/extraction terminology and CPV-adjacent discovery without relaxing semantic precision.

subject: Data annotation / AI training-data labeling
reason: Only one strict historical notice was found, but it is exceptionally on-thesis: Digital Africa's 'Data labeling service for AI hackathon competitions' explicitly requests high-quality consistent labeling to prepare datasets for model training/scoring. This is a market signal, not yet a broad market-size claim.
model_implication: If broader multilingual discovery finds recurrence, this is almost ideal for AI-assisted production + low-cost human validation.

subject: eDiscovery / legal document review
reason: 17 precision records exist, but all are flagged legal-specialist-risk. AI can compress review, but privilege, legal-supervision, jurisdiction and data-security requirements likely dominate SPM's native advantage.
